item.name: MCP circuit breaker cooldown + reconnect reset
item.contract: MCP tool calls maintain Hermes-compatible per-server recovery state: repeated call failures trip a circuit breaker, calls before cooldown short-circuit without touching the session, the first call after cooldown is a half-open probe, probe success closes the breaker, probe failure reopens it, and a successful OAuth reconnect clears stale breaker counts even if the immediate post-reconnect retry still fails.
item.degraded_mode: Tool call results report mcp_server_unreachable, mcp_breaker_open, mcp_half_open_failed, mcp_reconnect_required, or mcp_reconnect_reset evidence instead of hanging, hammering a broken server, or leaving a recovered server permanently disabled.
ready_when: MCP stdio/HTTP discovery, schema normalization, OAuth refresh, browser login, and managed gateway bridge rows are complete.
The tool-call execution path has a fake session seam where tests can inject success/failure without live MCP servers or subprocesses.
A fake clock can drive cooldown and half-open behavior deterministically.
not_ready_when: The slice opens real MCP stdio subprocesses, HTTP servers, browser OAuth, or token endpoints in unit tests.
Breaker reset waits for a successful post-reconnect tool call instead of resetting on the successful reconnect signal.
Shutdown and reconnect events race so reconnect wins over shutdown when both are set.

TestMCPCircuitBreakerHalfOpenFailureReopens proves a failed half-open probe re-arms cooldown and the next immediate call short-circuits.

TestMCPServerLifecycleEventShutdownWins proves shutdown has precedence over reconnect and reconnect events are cleared after use.
TestMCPProbeSkipsDisabledAndCleansUp proves the probe helper skips disabled servers and still closes loop/session resources on failures.
item.note: Complete: TDD added a Go-native MCP circuit breaker with per-server failure counts, cooldown-gated half-open probes, reconnect reset evidence, lifecycle reconnect/shutdown event precedence, and a fakeable probe helper that skips disabled servers and closes probe sessions. Managed gateway tool calls now route through the breaker and surface mcp_breaker_open/mcp_half_open_failed evidence without touching the gateway before cooldown.
done_signal: MCP fixtures prove cooldown/half-open/reopen behavior, reconnect reset, shutdown precedence, probe cleanup, and no live MCP/OAuth dependency.

provenance.note: Gormes has the MCP config/discovery/OAuth seams, but current progress did not track Hermes' call-level recovery state. The 2026-05-06 all-topic parity sweep confirmed managed gateway, OAuth refresh, and mcp login prerequisites are shipped, so the stale blocked_by metadata was removed for builder selection.

item.name: Auth state TOCTOU close + redaction default-on parity
item.contract: Gormes auth.json read-modify-write paths use atomic file replacement (open, write to sibling tempfile, fsync, rename) with no observable TOCTOU window between read and write. MCP OAuth credential persistence follows the same atomic-replace contract. The redaction default is restored to ON; opt-out is via explicit `redaction.enabled: false` in config. Mirrors Hermes v0.13.0 PRs #21193 (redaction default-on flip), #21194 (auth.json TOCTOU), #21241 (MCP OAuth TOCTOU). Reverts the v0.12.0 default-off flip (#16794).
item.degraded_mode: Without atomic replace, a concurrent read can observe a partially-written auth.json and crash the session; with the atomic-replace contract the read either sees the prior valid state or the new valid state, never a partial merge. Without redaction default-on, log capture, debug bundles, and trajectory writes leak credentials by default.

item.name: File write/patch staleness registry + cwd tracking

item.contract: Serialize concurrent file mutations that target the same canonical path across native write, edit, patch, and custom file-task tools while preserving parallel execution for independent files. Concurrent mutations to different files overlap or are not forced through a global lock.

item.name: Pre-execution command classification
item.contract: Classify every tool command as safe (whitelist), unsafe (blacklist), or uncertain (needs sandbox snapshot) before execution. Safe commands run directly. Unsafe commands are blocked. Uncertain commands trigger snapshot/rollback wrapper.
ready_when: Tool execution path is interceptable
Sandbox filesystem supports snapshots
not_ready_when: Tool execution cannot be intercepted
No sandbox filesystem available
acceptance: Commands classified as safe/unsafe/uncertain before execution
Safe commands execute directly with <1ms overhead
Unsafe commands are blocked with audit log entry
Uncertain commands trigger snapshot before execution
Classification rules are configurable per session
item.note: Complete: TDD expanded `CommandClassifier` from enum-only raw-string matching into detailed pre-execution decisions with command extraction, audit evidence, per-session configurable safe/unsafe rules, boundary-aware safe-prefix matching, and explicit safe/unsafe/uncertain actions. `ClassifyToolRequest` extracts `command`, `cmd`, `code`, or `script` from JSON tool input before execution, so terminal and execute_code requests are classified on the actual command body. `TransactionalExecutor` now records the classifier audit and marks `SnapshotTaken` before uncertain commands execute; unsafe commands remain blocked without invoking the inner executor.
done_signal: Classifier tests prove safe/unsafe/uncertain classification for representative command sets

evidence.note: Classifier and transactional executor fixtures prove safe/unsafe/uncertain classification, command extraction from terminal and execute_code tool inputs, configurable per-session rules, boundary-aware prefix matching, unsafe blocking, and snapshot-required audit evidence for uncertain commands.

item.name: Transactional tool execution with snapshot/rollback
item.contract: Wrap uncertain in-process tool calls with a bounded workspace filesystem snapshot before execution; successful calls commit by discarding the snapshot, while failed calls restore modified, deleted, and newly-created files before the executor returns.
ready_when: Pre-execution command classification is complete and marks uncertain tool requests as RequiresSnapshot.
The slice can use temp workspace fixtures and in-process fake tools; no live sandbox backend, shadow git repo, or provider credentials are required.
not_ready_when: The implementation tries to replace Hermes' full shadow-git checkpoint history, CLI /rollback UX, or sandbox isolation-depth policy in the same pass.
Rollback follows symlinks outside the workspace root, preserves new files created by failed tools, or deletes pre-existing files that should be restored.
acceptance: Uncertain tool calls create a workspace snapshot before invoking the inner executor.
Failed uncertain tool calls restore modified file content, restore files deleted during the call, and remove files created during the call.
Successful uncertain tool calls commit by preserving filesystem changes and reporting no rollback.
Safe tool calls do not pay snapshot cost, and unsafe tool calls remain blocked without touching the inner executor.
Rollback failures are returned as degraded executor errors instead of being hidden behind the tool failure.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-07: the bounded all-topic weakness sweep covered CLI/TUI, provider/auth, gateway/channels, tools, sessions/memory/Goncho, install/runtime, browser automation, docs/public, and release/operator rows. Planned row count was 66, so a new row was allowed, but this existing P1 row was the better completion-biased target: it already had local classifier/executor scaffolding, but its old contract was overbroad, cited speculative/nonlocal sandbox evidence, and was not actually builder-ready. TDD landed `internal/tools/snapshot.go` plus transactional executor wiring: uncertain tool requests with workspace_root metadata now snapshot regular files/directories/symlinks before execution, roll back modified/deleted/created files on failure, preserve successful changes on commit, keep safe/unsafe classifier behavior unchanged, and avoid following symlinks outside the workspace. Full shadow-git history, CLI rollback UX, and sandbox depth selection remain separate rows.
done_signal: Transactional executor tests prove rollback on failure and commit on success with filesystem integrity

item.name: MCP Streamable HTTP session lifecycle compatibility
item.contract: Extend the MCP HTTP client compatibility fixture to the current Streamable HTTP contract: initialize captures `Mcp-Session-Id`, all subsequent POST/GET/DELETE requests replay that header, SSE responses are accepted from the single MCP endpoint, 404 with a session header triggers a new initialization path, and legacy HTTP+SSE `/sse` endpoint events with `sessionId` are classified as backwards-compatibility input rather than silently dropping the session.

ready_when: MCP HTTP transport, OAuth refresh recovery, circuit breaker reconnect, and managed tool gateway bridge remain complete.
The worker can use httptest servers returning JSON and text/event-stream responses; no real MCP server or OAuth provider is required.
not_ready_when: The slice implements unrelated MCP sampling/tool schemas, starts a live MCP server, or changes stdio behavior.
The test relies on a network server outside httptest or assumes the removed 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE transport is the default transport.
acceptance: TestMCPStreamableHTTP_CapturesAndReplaysSessionID proves Initialize stores `Mcp-Session-Id` and ListTools/CallTool send it on subsequent requests.

TestMCPStreamableHTTP_ExpiredSessionReinitializes proves HTTP 404 with an existing session ID clears the session and returns typed evidence for reinitialize.

TestMCPLegacySSEEndpoint_SessionIDCompatibilityEvidence proves `/sse` endpoint events containing `/message?sessionId=...` are either upgraded into compatibility state or fail with explicit legacy_sse_unsupported evidence, never an empty sessionId POST.
TestMCPStreamableHTTP_DeleteSessionHeader proves Close or explicit termination sends DELETE with the stored session header when supported and tolerates 405.
done_signal: MCP HTTP fixtures prove session ID lifecycle, JSON/SSE single-endpoint behavior, expired-session recovery evidence, legacy SSE sessionId compatibility handling, and DELETE tolerance.
